title: Study on Radio Spectrum Policy Programme: taking stock and discussing future scenarios
description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure. 
In the context of spectrum management for the Digital Decade, the new (second) Radio Spectrum Policy Programme (RSPP) has been included in the Commission work programme for 2023, as a legislative initiative with an impact assessment. The Commission proposal for an RSPP is planned for adoption in the third quarter of 2023. The impact assessment will be supported by a study, which is the subject of this call for tenders. 
 

The strategic priorities of the EU-level spectrum policy are set in the currently applicable (first) RSPP, adopted in 2012. That RSPP forms part of a larger EU regulatory framework for spectrum, along with the 2002 Radio Spectrum Decision, that sets the principles for spectrum policy coordination and harmonized spectrum use in the EU, the 2018 European Electronic Communications Code, that includes provisions on coherent radio spectrum authorisation and integrates radio spectrum policy in the new European electronic communications framework.
The study will aim at taking stock of the application of the 2012 RSPP to date and further focus on assessing the future trends of radio spectrum policy. The contractor will be required to help identifying and describing the problems to be tackled, refining the objectives for EU action, formulating policy options and assessing their potential impacts, costs and benefits, as well as identifying a preferred option, and setting out how the expected results will be monitored and evaluated.
 

It is paramount to reflect new or emerging EU policy priorities including reinforcing EU safety and digital and political sovereignty in the policy principles and actions of the RSPP. A new RSPP will provide strategic planning for spectrum management at least up to 2030, by fostering spectrum governance, reinforcing the common market perspective, and ensuring effective and efficient spectrum management in support of the EU policy objectives (e.g. those set out in the European Green Deal, the New Industrial Strategy for Europe, the new Space Policy). It must contribute to the achievement of the ambitious Digital Decade targets, and focus on strategic policy needs (e.g., 6G, green deal, quantum, space, automated transport, IoT, WiFi, metaverse).
 

The study should also address the fragmentation of the EU-level spectrum market, which leads to (co-ordination) costs, undermines the incentives to invest in networks and impairs the provision of advanced connectivity devices and services. The diversity of authorisation practices (such as auction design) across the EU, especially in terms of setting prices, spectrum caps and timing, may adversely shape markets and hinder investment. There is a need, therefore, to reinforce a common market perspective of radio spectrum.
 

The study should explore how the digital transformation and in particular the evolving wireless communication needs are driving the growing demand for efficient and coherent spectrum management. The deployment of new technologies and mechanisms, such as Artificial Intelligence and automation techniques, can boost efficient spectrum use, e.g. through sharing and flexible licensing. Furthermore, the pan-European nature of services enabled by wireless communications, such as connected cars/trains or remote healthcare, calls for a coherent cross-border approach.

Total maximum value: € 100,000. Maximum contract duration: 5 months.

title: KOSMOS Festival 2025 - Technische Produktionsplanung und Koordination/ Realisierung
description: Der Anspruch der Ausschreibung besteht in der ganzheitlichen Planung und Umsetzung der Produktion des KOSMOS Festivals 2025. Inhaltlich gliedert sich das interdisziplinäre KOSMOS Festival 2025 in mehrere zentrale Themenbereiche. Neben Musik bilden Sport, Gesellschaft, Kunst und Wirtschaft eigenständige Säulen, die das Programm prägen und eine interdisziplinäre Vielfalt ermöglichen. Es wird ein Dienstleister zur Einrichtung der Veranstaltungsflächen einschließlich der vorgelagerten Ämterkommunikation, Veranstaltungskonzeption, Planung und Koordination sowie schließlich der technischen Durchführung des Festivals angefragt. Der Auftragsgegenstand umfasst neben der technischen Produktionsplanung und Koordination/ Realisierung des KOSMOS Festivals 2025 auch die Sicherheitskonzeption und Veranstaltungsleitung in Verbindung mit der Budgetkontrolle für die von dieser Ausschreibung erfassten Leistungen. Zur Erbringung dieser spezialisierten und umfassenden Dienstleistungen werden ein entsprechendes Know-How und einschlägige Erfahrung auf dem Gebiet der technischen Leistungen und Planungen für die Veranstaltungsbranche sowie eine gute Vernetzung mit den lokalen und regionalen Partnern und Beteiligten vorausgesetzt. Für eine reibungslose Umsetzung ist eine enge Zusammenarbeit mit der Kulturhauptstadt Europas Chemnitz 2025 gGmbH als Veranstalterin erforderlich. Die Anforderung der Leistungen kann im Einzelfall sehr kurzfristig erfolgen, auch weniger als 12 Stunden im Voraus. Eine direkte Reaktion auf solche Anfragen und eine gute Erreichbarkeit sind daher entscheidende Voraussetzungen für eine erfolgreiche Zusammenarbeit. Die Auftraggeberin ist und bleibt Veranstalterin des KOSMOS Festivals 2025. Für besondere Aufgaben beabsichtigen wir weitere selbstständige Unternehmer:innen zu beauftragen (insbesondere für die mediale Begleitung und Dokumentation), die auf den Veranstaltungs- und/ oder Festivalbetrieb spezialisiert sind. Insbesondere diese Aufträge sind nicht Gegenstand dieser Ausschreibung. Von der Ausschreibung ebenfalls ausgeschlossen ist der formale Akt der Flächenbeantragungen und der Abschluss von Versicherungen sowie die inhaltliche Gestaltung des Programms. Letzteres wird durch die Einbindung externer Teams aus der Stadtgesellschaft bewerkstelligt, die für die Kuration und die aktive Mitgestaltung verantwortlich sind. Zusammenarbeit und Abstimmung mit diesen anderen Unternehmer:innen, den kuratorischen Teams sowie die Einbindung von Vereinen, Verbänden, Unternehmen und Privatpersonen aus der Stadtgesellschaft sind zur Einhaltung der Zeitpläne und Sicherung des demokratischen Anliegens des Festivals zwingend. Kursorische Zusammenfassung der zu erbringenden Leistungen: • Projektplanung • Abfrage der Gewerke • Erstellung von Lageplan • Ablaufplanung • Einbindung von Gewerken und Institutionen • Termine und Absprachen mit Genehmigungsbehörden • Erstellung Verkehrskonzept • Grob-Planung der Gastronomie • Erstellung und Umsetzung des Sicherheitskonzeptes • Übernahme der Kommunikation zwischen Künstlern und Produktion • VA-Leitung vor Ort • VA-Umsetzung vor Ort • Technische Planung und Umsetzung von Eventflächen und Bühnen • Sicherheitskonzeption • Veranstaltungsleitung • Budgetkontrolle

title: Prize Contest ‘Sentinel Strike Challenge’
description: Categories Prizes Opening date05 May 2026 Closing date04 June 2026 .procurement_downloads { display: none; } PURPOSE OF THE PRIZE CONTESTEDA, through its Hub for European Defence Innovation (HEDI), has launched the Loitering Munitions “Sentinel Strike Challenge”, a Prize Contest designed to support the operational experimentation of emerging loitering munition capabilities in Europe.This initiative aims to:Generate operational evidence: Produce objective and comparable evidence on the performance, resilience, reliability, safety and operational suitability of complete loitering munition systems.Support Member States: Provide trusted evidence to support capability planning, requirement refinement and potential future cooperative activities.Test in realistic conditions: Assess systems in realistic, degraded and contested operational environments.Demonstrate complete systems: Enable selected industry participants to demonstrate full loitering munition systems under controlled military experimentation conditions.Strengthen defence innovation: Bring together operational users, technical experts, industry and national authorities to support Europe’s defence innovation ecosystem. SCOPE OF THE PRIZE CONTESTThe EDA invites applications for the operational experimentation of Class I Aerial Loitering Munitions, with:Maximum take-off mass: up to 25 kgOperational range: up to 40 kmParticipating systems will be assessed across the full precision strike mission cycle, including:Mission planningDeploymentLaunchTarget detection and identificationTarget trackingEngagementPost-strike assessmentThe Challenge will focus on complete loitering munition systems that combine intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance, navigation and precision strike functions within a single capability.PARTICIPATION PROCESSThe Prize Contest is structured in two stages.Stage 1 – Technical Proposal AssessmentEligible applicants will submit technical proposals for evaluation.Up to ten Stage 1 prizes may be awarded.The five highest-ranked Stage 1 winners will be invited to proceed to Stage 2.Stage 2 – Operational Experimentation CampaignSelected participants will deploy and demonstrate their systems during the operational experimentation campaign.Systems will be assessed during field experimentation and through final reports and experimentation results. The campaign is expected to take place in September - October 2026 in Portugal, within the framework of the HEDI Operational Experimentation Campaign 2026, in conjunction with the Portuguese Army’s ARTEX26 technological experimentation exercise. Trials are expected to be conducted at the Santa Margarida Military Training Area, including live-fire demonstrations. TARGET AUDIENCEThe Prize Contest is aimed at eligible industry participants capable of providing and demonstrating complete Class I Aerial Loitering Munition systems.The initiative is particularly relevant for companies developing loitering munition capabilities suitable for operational experimentation in realistic military environments and for observation by European defence stakeholders. IMPORTANT INFORMATIONThis is a Prize Contest, not a standard procurement procedure.The Challenge is intended to provide Member States with reliable, comparable operational evidence on loitering munition capabilities.The maximum total prize budget is EUR 2,000,000, divided as follows:Stage 1 prizes: up to EUR 200,000Stage 2 prizes: up to EUR 1,800,000Applications submitted after the deadline or sent to a different email address will be considered non-admissible.The Rules of Contest with full details, including eligibility requirements, technical admission criteria, award criteria and submission procedures, are available after registration. SUBMISSION DETAILS AND CONTACT POINTApplications must be submitted by email to:Prize.Contest@eda.europa.euThe deadline for receipt of applications is:Thursday, 04 June 2026 at 12:00 Brussels timeThe Prize Contest documentation is available for download through the EDA pre-registration link:Pre-registration for the Sentinel Strike Challenge Prize Contest INDICATIVE TIMETABLEJune 2026: Evaluation of Stage 1 applicationsJuly 2026: Notification of Stage 1 prize winners and invitations to Stage 2September-October 2026: Operational experimentation campaign in PortugalJanuary/February 2027: Award ceremony PROTECTION OF PERSONAL DATAProcessing of personal data for submission purposes is expected to comply with relevant EDA data protection regulations and policies, as further detailed in the Rules of Contest and related procurement documentation.
